content.text: Section 14.6 contains a substantive insurance covenant. Submitting.

input.quote: 14.6 Insurance. Each Party shall procure and maintain insurance, including product liability insurance, with respect to its activities hereunder and under the Ancillary Agreements and which is consistent with normal business practices of companies similarly situated at all times during which any SHP2 Inhibitors or Product is being clinically tested in human subjects or commercially distributed or sold. Sanofi may fulfill such obligation through self- insurance. Each Party shall provide the other Party with evidence of such insurance upon request
input.rationale: An insurance clause is present (Section 14.6), so the rule's "missing" trigger is not met. RevMed is bound to procure and maintain insurance — expressly including product liability cover, the line most relevant to a clinical/commercial collaboration of this kind — at levels consistent with normal business practices of similarly situated companies, for the whole period during which SHP2 Inhibitors or Product are in human clinical testing or commercial distribution. The clause also delivers the two mechanics the playbook cares about beyond limits: evidence of insurance on request, and (one-way in our favour) advance written notice from RevMed of cancellation, non-renewal or material change. It further confirms that insurance does not cap either Party's Article XIV indemnification obligations, preserving our recovery against RevMed. Several terms run in our favour and should not be flagged: the obligation is mutual, and Sanofi alone may satisfy it through self-insurance. On its material terms this sits at the fallback rather than the preferred position. Noted but not flagged: there are no stated dollar limits (no CGL 1M/2M, no E&O, no cyber/privacy tower) and no one-year tail after the term. Those preferred-position specifics are of limited weight here because RevMed is a licensor/co-development counterparty rather than a hosting or data-processing vendor — it does not host our systems or work on our premises, so the walk-away scenario (no insurance for a vendor processing personal data or working on-site) is not engaged. Per the playbook's classification semantics, these are sub-elements short of preferred wording and are recorded in the rationale rather than redlined.
